description: A transfusion medicine director must allocate the hospital's one available specialized platelet unit among three patients and finalize the product, timing, post-transfusion testing, and delivery plan, with input from hematology, the blood bank, procedural services, and courier operations.

shared_context.S1: The hospital has one available specialized platelet unit and three patients, K, L, and M, whose teams have requested it.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Chen makes the final allocation and documents the transfusion plan.
shared_context.S3: The unit is being held in the regional blood center's controlled inventory until the hospital confirms the recipient and delivery plan.
shared_context.S4: The hospital's daily transfusion huddle includes hematology, the blood bank, procedural services, and courier operations before a blood product allocation is finalized.

PF1.text: Patient K's platelet count is 8, and a lumbar puncture is planned today; the hematology protocol requires the platelet count to be raised to at least 50 before that procedure, making K the patient who must receive this unit.

PF2.text: Patient K's transplant protocol requires an irradiated, leukoreduced, HLA-matched platelet product, and the available unit meets all three specifications; the blood bank cannot substitute an ordinary pooled platelet product for this order.

PF3.text: Patient K's lumbar puncture is booked for 15:00, and procedural services requires a post-transfusion platelet count at exactly 14:30 before the procedure can proceed; the transfusion must therefore be scheduled to start at 13:00.

PF4.text: The regional blood center has confirmed a validated medical-courier handoff that will deliver the unit to the hospital blood bank at exactly 12:45; courier operations needs that delivery commitment recorded before releasing the unit.

acceptance_conditions: The specialized platelet unit must be assigned to patient K.
The product must be documented as irradiated, leukoreduced, and HLA-matched.
The transfusion must be scheduled to start at 13:00.
A post-transfusion platelet count must be scheduled for exactly 14:30.
The regional blood-center delivery at exactly 12:45 must be recorded as a courier commitment.
The hematology finding requiring K to receive the unit must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C2: decisions['product_specification'] in ['irradiated, leukoreduced, HLA-matched platelet product', 'Irradiated, leukoreduced, HLA-matched platelet product', 'irradiated leukoreduced HLA matched platelet product', 'irradiated, leukoreduced, HLA-matched', 'Irradiated, leukoreduced, HLA-matched']
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] in ['platelet_delivery', 'delivery_confirmation', 'delivery_coordination', 'courier_delivery'] and '12:45' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Patient K's platelet count of 8 and required pre-procedure threshold of 50 change the recipient from an unresolved choice among K, L, and M to K and require that clinical finding to support the allocation.
K's transplant protocol changes the product specification from an unspecified platelet product to exactly irradiated, leukoreduced, and HLA-matched.
The 15:00 procedure and required 14:30 count change the transfusion timing to exactly 13:00 and the testing time to exactly 14:30.
The confirmed regional-courier handoff changes the delivery plan from no documented release arrangement to a hospital blood-bank delivery commitment at exactly 12:45.
